title: 2012 HMMT February Guts Problem 10
statement: Let \(P\) be a polynomial such that \(P(x)=P(0)+P(1) x+P(2) x^{2}\) and \(P(-1)=1\). Compute \(P(3)\).

solutions.text: 5 Plugging in \(x=-1,1,2\) results in the trio of equations \(1=P(-1)=P(0)-P(1)+P(2)\), \(P(1)=P(0)+P(1)+P(2) \Rightarrow P(1)+P(2)=0\), and \(P(2)=P(0)+2 P(1)+4 P(2)\). Solving these as a system of equations in \(P(0), P(1), P(2)\) gives \(P(0)=-1, P(1)=-1, P(2)=1\). Consequently, \(P(x)=x^{2}-x-1 \Rightarrow P(3)=5\).
